previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis and a history of coronary artery disease was admitted due to bilateral leg swelling and pain, with mild shortness of breath en route to the hospital. Evaluation revealed significant fluid overload, evidenced by a weight gain of 3 kg above dry weight and a markedly elevated BNP level. A chest X-ray showed moderate to severe pulmonary edema. The patient underwent ultrafiltration, removing 2.8 liters of fluid, after which his symptoms resolved. He remained stable, with improved breathing and reduced leg discomfort, and was discharged home with instructions on daily weight monitoring and fluid management. Follow-up was arranged with his primary care provider.
